title: Entropy Forge — a lossless compression lab
description: An interactive information-theory and data-compression laboratory, built from scratch with zero dependencies. It measures Shannon entropy (order-0/1/2) and the theoretical compression floor, then implements and visualises every major lossless codec family — a Huffman coder with a live code-tree and canonical length table; a genuine Witten–Neal–Cleary integer arithmetic coder (32-bit registers, E1/E2/E3 renormalisation, pending-bit underflow) with adaptive order-0 and order-1 models that hug the entropy bound; LZ77/LZSS sliding-window matching with a colour-coded parse map; LZW with a self-building dictionary and variable-width codes (KwKwK handled); and a full bzip2-style Burrows–Wheeler pipeline (suffix-sorted BWT with LF-mapping inverse, move-to-front, run-length, arithmetic). Composite codecs assemble the real formats — DEFLATE-lite (LZ77 tokens entropy-coded) and bzip-lite — and a Benchmark page races all seven on seven corpora against the entropy floor, every result verified by a full decode. A live Self-test round-trips every codec across the corpus plus adversarial edge cases (empty, single-symbol, all-256-bytes, long runs, pseudo-random); an offline fuzz of 2,800 cases across sizes to 9,000 bytes and full alphabets found zero mismatches.
